title: Variant Comparator Playbook for Gradual Adoption and Auto-Rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a defensible, repeatable product playbook and lightweight control plane to run A/B style comparisons between model versions with constrained exposure, automated sequential statistical checks, and automated rollback triggers. This ticket covers: experiment setup templates, exposure budgets, shadow-run harness for offline validation, a comparator metric set, sequential stopping rules (both frequentist and Bayesian options), and an operational runbook for on-call and SRE during canaries. Goal: enable product and platform teams to run safe, fast model upgrades with measurable risk bounds and predictable cost and latency impact.
acceptance_criteria: Template-based experiment creation in Console (name, cohorts, exposure ramp, metrics)
Exposure budget enforcement with hard caps and time windows (per-variant)
Two-stop rule options implemented: Bayesian credible-interval guard and sequential p-value with alpha-spending
Shadow traffic pipeline that mirrors 100% of requests to candidate model without affecting client latency
Auto-rollback hook based on tolerances for primary metric drop and increased error-rate above threshold
Audit trail in Console with experiment timeline, metric deltas, and final decision recorded
Integration tests covering scheduler, metric ingestion, and rollback enactment
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Offline verification — run candidate on a shadow harness for 48–72h against golden prompt set (functional regressions, safety filters)
Phase 1: Micro-canary — 0.5% user traffic for 2h, monitor latency, 5 core metrics; hard stop on latency > +150ms or error-rate +0.5%
Phase 2: Graduated exposure — 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% over 24–72 hours with sequential checks at each step
Phase 3: Cohort ramping — open exposure to targeted cohorts (beta users, geo/region), run for at least one daily traffic cycle
Phase 4: Promote or rollback — auto-promote when pre-specified sequential criteria met for three consecutive checks; trigger automated rollback on breach
Post-mortem: Automatic capture of prompts, top failing queries, and PR link for root-cause analysis
statistical_checks: Primary metric: signed difference with bootstrap CI (95%); require lower bound >= -0.5% for safe promotion
Secondary metrics: latency p95, API error-rate, hallucination-rate proxy (synthetic checks) — simple threshold checks
Sequential rule: alpha-spending using O'Brien-Fleming schedule with max alpha=0.05
Bayesian rule: require 95% posterior probability that candidate >= control on utility score using Beta/Binomial or Gaussian model as appropriate
Drift detection: CUSUM on important distributional features (length, token distribution) with configurable sensitivity
Minimum sample requirement: 10k inference events per variant or a time floor of 6 hours (whichever is first)
implementation_notes: Use existing metric ingestion pipeline (ENG-44221) and extend tags for experiment_id and cohort
Expose experiment creation API to SDKs for infra-as-code (console + CLI + infra templates)
Reuse Redwood Optimize heuristics for suggested exposure ramps based on expected QPS and latency SLOs
Auto-rollback should call route-control API to pin traffic back to last stable model and open a rollback incident in PagerDuty
Keep experiment metadata immutable after creation for auditability (start_time, specs)
